candidate_relations.reason: Broad-based budding yeast in bronchoalveolar lavage and dense upper-lobe consolidation establish pulmonary blastomycosis, but the label omits the ipsilateral ptosis-miosis syndrome caused by it.
The lavage shows broad-based budding yeast and the urine Blastomyces antigen is positive, rather than the cystic organisms or immunosuppressed setting expected for Pneumocystis pneumonia.
Coronary disease, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure are pre-existing conditions and do not explain the fungal upper-lobe consolidation with new right ptosis and miosis.
Minnesota exposure and broad-based budding yeast support Blastomyces, not the spherules of Coccidioides associated with pulmonary coccidioidomycosis.
The positive Blastomyces antigen and broad-based budding yeast support blastomycosis, but this broad label leaves out both pneumonia and the secondary Horner syndrome.
Tuberculosis testing was negative while bronchoalveolar lavage directly demonstrated broad-based budding yeast, excluding tuberculous pneumonia as the recorded cause.
No lymphadenopathy or systemic tumor was found, and the lung process has organism-level evidence for Blastomyces rather than lymphoma.
An upper-lobe lesion with Horner signs can mimic a Pancoast tumor, but lavage yeast and positive Blastomyces antigen identify invasive fungal pneumonia without a demonstrated neoplasm.
Symptoms progressed despite antibiotics given for bronchitis, and imaging plus fungal microscopy subsequently showed multilobar blastomycotic pneumonia.
Blastomycotic pneumonia matches the dense consolidation and broad-based budding yeast, but does not include the new right ptosis and miosis that complete the reference diagnosis.
